payload.instructions: Preserve all candidate IDs and distinctions. Broader parent themes organize evidence; they do not imply measurement equivalence.

themes.disagreements: contradictions, weak signals, and proxy distinctions
evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.interpretation: common or complementary evidence
themes.name: theme

themes.disagreements: Effect modification signals are present but moderate (support fractions ~0.4), suggesting their role as confounders may be equally prominent.
themes.interpretation: Measurements regarding the presence and size of adrenal nodules show consistent evidence of influence on treatment assignment, outcome prognosis, and effect modification.
themes.name: Adrenal-related Indicators

themes.disagreements: Age is an overwhelming confounder, whereas history of AKI shows only a weak signal for effect modification and minimal prognostic value.
themes.interpretation: Core patient characteristics, most notably age, exhibit powerful evidence as confounders affecting both treatment and outcome.
themes.name: Patient Demographics and Comorbidities

themes.disagreements: ALC has negligible treatment signal but strong effect modification evidence; ANC is strongly prognostic and moderately linked to treatment.
themes.interpretation: Absolute counts of lymphocytes and neutrophils show divergence, with lymphocytes acting as potential effect modifiers and neutrophils as confounders.
themes.name: Hematological Parameters

themes.disagreements: Acetaminophen administration is primarily a confounder, while adjuvant chemotherapy is a strong candidate for effect modification.
themes.interpretation: Previous administration of medications or chemotherapy shows a split between simple confounding and heterogeneous treatment effects.
themes.name: Prior Therapeutic Interventions

themes.disagreements: Airway involvement is a moderate confounder/modifier; actionable molecular alterations provide very weak signals across all roles.
themes.interpretation: Indicators of disease location and genetic actionability show varied importance, with airway involvement being more prominent than molecular markers.
themes.name: Anatomic and Molecular Markers

themes.disagreements: Causal forest evidence for ambulation status suggests a moderate effect signal, though the overwhelming strength of the main effects dominates the role reconciliation.
themes.interpretation: Strong and consistent evidence across multiple model families for both treatment prediction and outcome prognosis, indicating a likely confounding role.
themes.name: Functional and Respiratory Baseline

themes.disagreements: ALT (016) exhibits a much stronger treatment prediction signal than ALP (015), yet both share similar support fractions in causal forest evidence.
themes.interpretation: These candidates show moderate to strong treatment prediction signals, but weak outcome signals, with complementary evidence for treatment-heterogeneity from R-learners and Causal Forests.
themes.name: Hepatic Function Markers

themes.disagreements: The mutation status (013) has stronger causal forest support than the rearrangement status (014), which shows virtually no support in the same family.
themes.interpretation: Evidence identifies mutation status as a potential effect modifier, while rearrangement status serves as a weaker, correlated proxy with negligible independent signal.
themes.name: Genomic ALK Status

themes.disagreements: Alcohol use (012) shows a confounder pattern, whereas antidiabetic use (020) is primarily an instrument-like predictor of treatment without outcome or effect signals.
themes.interpretation: A diverse group where some members act as confounders (alcohol use) or purely prognostic factors (anemia type), while others show moderate evidence for effect modification (anticoagulant use).
themes.name: Comorbidities and Lifestyle Factors

themes.disagreements: Differences in signal strength between univariable and penalized models; atorvastatin_dose is a far more dominant treatment predictor than ast_level or antihypertensive_use.
themes.interpretation: Cardiovascular and metabolic markers showing strong association with treatment assignment and some prognostic value, suggesting a confounding role.
themes.name: Cardiovascular and Metabolic Profile

themes.disagreements: Anxiety shows strong heterogeneity signals (R-learner/Causal Forest), while appetite status is almost exclusively a prognostic factor.
themes.interpretation: Psychosocial and general health indicators that influence outcome prognosis, with some evidence for treatment-effect heterogeneity for anxiety.
themes.name: Psychosocial and General Well-being

themes.disagreements: High variance in signal quality; axial_structure_abnormality is robust, whereas atrial_fibrillation and audiogram_status are very weak or non-evaluable.
themes.interpretation: Structural abnormalities and specific medical history markers showing mixed evidence, with some acting as effect modifiers or prognostic factors.
themes.name: Structural and Historical Medical Findings

themes.disagreements: Causal forest and R-learner show strong effect modification for BUN, while GFR and BP are more clearly confounders.
themes.interpretation: High-confidence physiological and renal indicators that strongly predict both treatment assignment and outcome.
themes.name: Renal and Cardiovascular Vitals

themes.disagreements: Predictive forest shows strong outcome signals for weight and biopsy method, but these are not replicated in univariable or penalized models.
themes.interpretation: Biomarkers and procedural details that appear primarily to influence prognosis or treatement response heterogeneity.
themes.name: Biomarkers and Clinical Procedures

themes.disagreements: Consistent moderate signals in predictive forests across anthropometrics, but lack of strong univariable significance.
themes.interpretation: General physical characteristics with weak-to-moderate predictive value across roles.
themes.name: Anthropometrics and Body State

themes.disagreements: Signals are generally sparse and lack cross-method consistency.
themes.interpretation: Prior medication history with insufficient evidence to establish a causal role.
themes.name: Prior Medication History

themes.disagreements: Treatment signals are primarily captured by predictive forests rather than univariable models, indicating non-linear dependencies.
themes.interpretation: Measurements related to the presence, characteristics, and symptomatic location of bone metastases show strong prognostic signals for outcome and moderate signals for treatment prediction, suggesting roles as confounders.
themes.name: Skeletal Metastasis Burden

themes.disagreements: The magnitude of the effect modification signal is generally higher for lesion count and edema than for lesion size.
themes.interpretation: Measurements of brain lesion count, size, and associated edema demonstrate strong prognostic importance and significant evidence of effect modification across multiple models (Causal Forest, R-learner).
themes.name: Intracranial Lesion Severity

themes.disagreements: Low support in univariable outcome models contrast with high support in the Causal Forest.
themes.interpretation: Bone pain status shows weak prognostic signal but a strong signal for treatment effect heterogeneity in the Causal Forest, suggesting a primary role as an effect modifier.
themes.name: Symptomatic Bone Pain

themes.disagreements: Small fragments of support in R-learners are not corroborated by other model families.
themes.interpretation: Procedural markers (bolus confirmation, vaccination) and BRAF mutation status show inconsistent or weak signals across all modeling axes.
themes.name: Clinical/Molecular Metadata

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
